main_body: Snow-covered log cabin: a large snow-covered roof slope (rows 8-35) over a log front wall with a plank door and two shuttered windows (rows 36-62)
top_band: Snow roof slope, lightest tones #f6f9fd/#dce5f1 with blue-grey shading, rows 8-35 at x=32, ending in a bluish step at rows 34-35 and a dark eave at rows 36-38
evidence: The roof is drawn as a big foreshortened surface seen from above, as in the Beodeul house references, which also show their roofs as large slopes. A snow-edge step (rows 34-35, L 130-166) marks the front edge. Under it come dark eave rows 36-38 with icicles, then the log wall with a framed door, shutters and windows set back under the overhang. The roof and wall both satisfy the contract, and no receding side face is drawn.

style.evidence: The snow ramp has about 5 steps (#f6f9fd, #dce5f1, #bccade, #97a8c6, #7383a8) with clumpy, mottled shading. The wood has several browns, with log ends, plank grain, iron straps and a lit orange window glow. Outlines are tinted dark blue (#21283f) beside snow and dark brown (#362016) beside wood, with 0% near-neutral dark edge pixels. Flat-fill coverage is 0%. Median colours per tile (17) match house-h101_0 (18) and exceed house-h112_0-stone (11). The total of 37 distinct colours is lower than the references, but that follows from the locked, narrow snow palette and does not make the tiles thin. It would sit next to the references without looking flatter or more sticker-like.
